model.name: Geometry / Coordinate Reference
model.purpose: Give any subject a defensible spatial expression: geometry, the coordinate reference system and epoch that make its coordinates meaningful, the ordered coordinate operations that relate one referencing context to another, and the accuracy, uncertainty and outcome statements that qualify the result.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-033 is a mixin attached to a host subject. It owns how coordinates and geometry are expressed and related: geometry type and coordinate dimension; the coordinate reference system carried as a governed reference; the coordinate epoch for dynamic reference frames; the ordered chain of conversions, transformations, point-motion and concatenated operations that relate a source referencing context to a target one, with method, parameter, external-resource and toolchain pins sufficient to reproduce a derived geometry; axis, unit and dimensionality normalization; geometry-shape treatment such as densification, clipping, longitude wrapping and antimeridian handling; and the stated operation accuracy, positional uncertainty, precision, resolution and explicit outcome or exception declarations that qualify every derived coordinate. It does not define coordinate reference systems, operation methods, parameter values or their accuracy statements, does not execute operations, and does not acquire or host correction resources.
in_scope: Geometry representation of a subject: geometry role, coordinate tuples, coordinate dimension and any height or measure ordinate.
Declaration of the coordinate reference system by governed reference rather than by local redefinition, including compound and interpolation CRS references.
Coordinate epoch and dynamic-reference-frame temporal qualification of coordinates.
Ordered coordinate-operation chains (conversion, transformation, point-motion, concatenated) with method, parameter, direction and step-order pins.
External resource pins: grid, triangulated-network and deformation-model identity, version and checksum, plus transformation-engine and registry-dataset version pins.
Stated operation accuracy, positional uncertainty, numeric precision and coordinate resolution attached to coordinates and derived geometry.
Axis order, unit and dimensionality normalization, and geometry-shape treatment including densification, clipping, wrapping, antimeridian and polar handling.
Preservation of original geometry and original CRS alongside any derived geometry, with lineage sufficient for reproduction.
Explicit outcome and exception declarations, including ballpark or fallback status, out-of-area coordinates, missing resources, epoch mismatch, invalid geometry, tolerance breach and lossy export.
out_of_scope: Definition, maintenance, deprecation and supersession of coordinate reference systems, datums, operation methods, parameter values and their stated accuracies, which are owned by geodetic parameter registries.
Execution of coordinate operations and the runtime environment of transformation engines, including runtime candidate ranking, caching, concurrency and error recovery.
Acquisition, hosting, licensing, redistribution and retraction of grid, triangulated-network and deformation-model resources.
Survey adjustment, GNSS processing and sensor observation models that produce the original coordinates in the first place.
Spatial indexing, spatial query evaluation, topology repair engines and cartographic rendering or styling.
The host subject's business identity, lifecycle, authority and permissions; the mixin attaches to a host and never replaces it.
Storage encodings and access interfaces, which are projections of this model rather than its semantics.
Audit-trail construction, retention execution and enforcement of access decisions, which belong to the adopting Dimension's governance facilities.

boundary_notes.distinction: The parent owns place identity, spatial-context semantics and how a subject relates to named places. This mixin owns only the coordinate expression of geometry and the operations and quality statements that qualify it. The parent boundary was not supplied as a relation rationale and is recorded as an unresolved boundary.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Geodetic parameter registry (EPSG Dataset, OGC definitions server)
boundary_notes.distinction: The registry defines and versions CRSs, operation methods, parameter values, extents, stated accuracies and deprecation state. This model cites those definitions by code or URI and adds only subject-specific pins; it never restates or overrides a registry definition and never owns its lifecycle.

The engine owns execution, runtime ranking of candidate operations, resource resolution and its own release lifecycle. This model records the declared chain and an engine version pin so a result can be reproduced; it holds no execution, enforcement or audit-trail semantics.

The distributor owns hosting, licensing, availability and content. This model holds resource identity, version and a content checksum, and reports unavailability as an outcome rather than attempting acquisition.

The quality model owns measure definitions, evaluation procedures and conformance levels. This model binds accuracy and uncertainty values to a specific geometry and operation chain and states when they are unknown.

Encodings own serialization constraints such as a fixed default CRS, axis order rules and antimeridian splitting. This model stays format-neutral and records which encoding rule was applied as a treatment declaration.

sources.title: OGC Abstract Specification Topic 2: Referencing by coordinates
sources.version_or_date: Version 5.0.1 (OGC 18-005r5), adopting the ISO 19111:2019 conceptual schema
sources.relevance: Normative definitions of coordinate operation, conversion versus transformation, concatenated operation, point motion operation, coordinate epoch, coordinate set, datum ensemble, operation method and parameters, source and target CRS, operation accuracy and domain of validity.

sources.title: PROJ documentation — Coordinate operations
sources.relevance: Working classification of operations into projections, conversions and transformations, and the note that projections are conversions under the standards but are treated separately in practice.

sources.title: PROJ documentation — Transformation pipelines (+proj=pipeline)
sources.relevance: Ordered step declaration, global versus per-step parameters, the +inv step modifier, omit_fwd/omit_inv, and the constraint that a pipeline without a forward path cannot be constructed.

sources.title: PROJ documentation — projinfo
sources.relevance: Area-of-interest spatial tests (contains/intersects), crs-extent-use strategies, grid-check strategies for missing grids, minimum-accuracy filtering, pivot CRS policy, superseded operations and ballpark suppression.

sources.title: PROJ documentation — Glossary
sources.relevance: Definition of a ballpark transformation as an operation that accounts only for axis order, unit and prime meridian differences, attempts no datum shift, and has unknown accuracy that can reach hundreds of metres.

sources.title: PROJ documentation — Resource files
sources.relevance: Grid resource formats for horizontal and vertical correction, the versioned PROJ-data resource package, network retrieval from a content delivery network, and resource search-path resolution.

sources.title: PROJ documentation — Transformations (usage)
sources.relevance: Chaining elementary operations so that the output of one is the input of the next, four-dimensional spatiotemporal coordinates with a time ordinate, and explicit handling of optional or missing grids including a null zero-shift grid.

sources.title: PROJ documentation — Transformation operations catalogue
sources.relevance: Enumeration of transformation methods showing which are grid-based (horizontal, vertical, geocentric and triangulated-network shifts) and which are time-dependent (deformation model, kinematic datum shift).

sources.title: RFC 7946 — The GeoJSON Format
sources.relevance: Single fixed CRS with longitude-latitude order, optional third elevation ordinate with a caution against further elements, antimeridian cutting rule for geometries, antimeridian bounding-box convention, and coordinate-precision guidance.

sources.title: OGC API - Features - Part 2: Coordinate Reference Systems by Reference
sources.relevance: Requirement that every CRS be referenceable by URI, the storage CRS concept, default CRS84 and CRS84h identifiers, assertion of the CRS used in a response, and the recommendation to publish a coordinate epoch for a dynamic storage CRS because coordinates without it are ambiguous.

sources.title: OGC Features and Geometries JSON - Part 1: Core
sources.relevance: CRS carried by reference with an optional decimal-year epoch, compound CRS by reference array, the duality of a primary geometry in its own CRS alongside a fallback geometry in a fixed CRS, and deferral of axis order to the closest-to-scope CRS metadata.

sources.title: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset — Guidance Notes
sources.organization: International Association of Oil & Gas Producers (IOGP) Geomatics Committee
sources.version_or_date: Index listing Guidance Note 7-1 v9 (Mar 2025), 7-2 v74 (Jul 2026), 7-3 v1.0 (Jul 2022), 7-5 v1.1 (May 2022), 7-6 v1.1 (Jun 2025), 7-7 v1 (Apr 2026)
sources.relevance: Authoritative registry publication set for coordinate conversion and transformation formulas, dataset content and maintenance, dataset management policy, and the specific treatment of null and copy transformations used as fallbacks.

sources.title: NGS Coordinate Conversion and Transformation Tool (NCAT)
sources.relevance: Authoritative statement that grid-based transformations provide local error estimates per transformation, that transformations are not supported outside the boundaries of the supported regions, and that orthometric and ellipsoidal height types are not interconverted by the transformation tool.

sources.title: New Datums — modernization of the National Spatial Reference System
sources.relevance: Plate-fixed terrestrial reference frames defined mathematically relative to a global frame, replacement of a levelling-based vertical datum by a geopotential datum realized with a geoid model, and the resulting need to qualify coordinates by frame and time.

sources.title: NADCON 5.0: Geometric Transformation Tool for points in the National Spatial Reference System (NOAA Technical Report NOS NGS 63)
sources.relevance: Documents a rebuilt grid-based transformation set of 44 separate transformations across nine regions, establishing that transformations are region-scoped, versioned resources rather than a single global function.

bundles.name: Coordinate Operation Chain and Reproducibility
bundles.description: Everything needed to state, without ambiguity, which referencing context a coordinate came from, which it was moved to, by which ordered operations and pinned resources, and how the original can still be recovered.
bundles.rationale: A coordinate operation is defined by its source and target coordinate reference systems, optionally its source and target coordinate epochs, a method with parameter values, and a domain of validity. Chains of such operations are themselves operations. Unless each of those elements is pinned, a derived geometry cannot be interpreted or reproduced, and the difference between a rigorous transformation and an unknown-accuracy fallback is invisible.

bundles.name: Accuracy, Normalization and Declared Outcomes
bundles.description: How good the resulting coordinates are, how they were normalized and reshaped, and what must be told to a consumer before the result is trusted.
bundles.rationale: A coordinate operation carries a stated accuracy, and empirically derived transformation parameters transfer their error into the output. Grid-based transformations supply local error estimates and are bounded by supported regions. Axis order, units and dimensionality differ between referencing contexts and encodings, and encoding rules force geometry-level treatment such as antimeridian splitting and precision limits. None of this is inferable from the coordinates alone, so it must be declared.

data_elements.name: Densification tolerance
data_elements.description: Maximum permitted deviation between the densified and the true transformed curve.

data_elements.name: Polar and singularity treatment note
data_elements.description: Declared handling near poles and projection singularities, including an explicit gap where no rule is authoritative.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are declarations about what was done to one geometry, meaningful only next to that geometry and its lineage. They are recorded inline as treatment codes and tolerances; the reshaped geometry itself is the host's data, not an artifact this mixin owns. Densification tolerance and polar handling rest on practice rather than a normative source and are flagged as a gap.

layers.name: Declared Outcomes and Exceptions
layers.description: The single outcome status of an applied chain, the named exceptions that may qualify it, and the limits that must be stated before a consumer relies on the result.

findings.name: Outcome status, exception taxonomy and lossy or round-trip declaration
findings.description: One coded status per applied chain, the named exception set that can accompany it, the tolerance actually tested, and an honest statement of round-trip and export limits.

answer_data: Outcome status code (succeeded, succeeded with qualifications, refused)
Observation timestamp of the outcome
Reference to the chain declaration the outcome belongs to

Affected step index or ordinate per exception

Observed residual or deviation
Breach verdict and the party who set the tolerance

Reasons reversibility is not guaranteed, such as grid interpolation, iteration or rounding
Measured round-trip residual where one was computed

Fitness statement scoped to a named purpose
Pointer to the original geometry and CRS

data_elements.name: Chain outcome status
data_elements.description: Single coded status for the applied chain.

data_elements.name: Exception code
data_elements.description: Named exception raised during the chain, with the step or ordinate it applies to.

data_elements.name: Tolerance breach indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the observed residual exceeded the declared tolerance.

data_elements.name: Round-trip claim
data_elements.description: What, if anything, is claimed about reversing the chain, and why exactness is not claimed.

data_elements.name: Lossy export note
data_elements.description: Statement of what an export dropped or rounded, such as a height ordinate, an epoch or decimal places.

data_elements.name: Outcome observation timestamp
data_elements.description: When the outcome was evaluated and recorded, kept separate from the geometry's event time.

artifacts.name: Coordinate transformation report
artifacts.description: The record issued for one applied chain that states its outcome status, exceptions, accuracy and uncertainty summary, and any lossy-export or round-trip qualification, so a consumer can judge fitness without re-deriving anything.
media_or_form: message payload attached to a derived geometry
artifacts.identity_strategy: No external master system issues an identifier for a locally produced report, so a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID is used. The report references the chain declaration, resource pins and original geometry rather than repeating them; the observation timestamp is metadata and never the identifier.

functions.name: Assemble declared operation chain record
functions.description: Build a complete, ordered chain declaration from supplied endpoint references, operation references, method and parameter pins, and report which pins are missing. Records only; performs no coordinate evaluation and queries no registry at run time.
inputs: Source and target CRS references
Optional source and target coordinate epochs
Ordered operation references with method and parameter values
Step directions and any interpolation CRS reference
outputs: Chain declaration record with ordered steps
Pin completeness report listing missing method, parameter or direction values
preconditions: Both endpoint CRS references are governed and resolvable
Every step carries an explicit index and direction
effects: Emits a chain declaration and a completeness report
Does not transform coordinates, rank candidate operations at run time, or alter registry-held definitions

functions.name: Validate area-of-use applicability
functions.description: Compare the subject geometry extent with the declared area of use of every step under a stated spatial test and report the applicability outcome.
inputs: Subject geometry extent
Declared area of use per step
Spatial test selection (contains or intersects)
outputs: Applicability outcome code per step and for the chain
List of steps whose extent does not cover the subject
preconditions: At least one step declares an area of use, or the absence is recorded explicitly
effects: Reports an out-of-area outcome when coverage fails
Does not suppress, substitute or re-select an operation

functions.name: Validate coordinate epoch consistency
functions.description: Determine whether an epoch is required by either endpoint, whether the supplied epochs are consistent with the chain, and whether a point-motion step is needed.
inputs: Dynamic-frame flags for both endpoints
Source and target coordinate epochs
Step list including any point-motion or deformation step
outputs: Epoch-missing or epoch-mismatch exception where applicable
preconditions: Endpoint CRS references are resolved sufficiently to know whether each frame is dynamic
effects: Reports epoch adequacy and required point-motion steps
Never silently assumes a default epoch; any assumption must be supplied and attributed

functions.name: Verify external resource and toolchain pins
functions.description: Check that every grid, triangulated-network or deformation-model dependency carries an identifier, version and checksum, and that engine and registry version pins are present and internally consistent.
inputs: Resource identifiers, versions and checksums
Recomputed checksum values where a local copy is presented
Engine version and registry dataset version pins
outputs: Pin verification report with verified, unverified and mismatched states
preconditions: The chain declaration names which steps depend on an external resource
effects: Reports integrity and completeness of pins
Never downloads, installs, licenses or redistributes a resource; acquisition stays with the distribution service

functions.name: Calculate conservative chain accuracy and uncertainty summary
functions.description: Derive a single accuracy and uncertainty summary for the chain from per-step stated values and any supplied local error estimates, forcing an unknown result whenever a step lacks a published value or is a fallback.
inputs: Stated accuracy per step with units
Local error estimates supplied with a resource, where available
Ballpark or fallback flags
outputs: Chain accuracy value and unit, or an unknown-accuracy declaration
Uncertainty summary with component split and stated basis
preconditions: The aggregation rule and its conservatism assumption are declared
effects: Emits an accuracy and uncertainty summary marked as a local computation, not an authority statement
Sets the unknown-accuracy flag when any step is unquantified

functions.name: Validate axis, unit and dimensionality declarations
functions.description: Compare the written axis order, ordinate units and coordinate dimension with the endpoint CRS definitions and the applicable encoding rule, and report ambiguity or unsupported dimensionality.
inputs: Written axis order and its claimed authority
Ordinate units and coordinate dimension
Endpoint CRS axis and unit definitions
Encoding profile rule in force
preconditions: The encoding profile whose axis rule applies is named
effects: Reports mismatches between CRS-defined and written axis order or units
Does not reorder, reproject or rewrite coordinates

functions.name: Validate residuals against declared tolerance
functions.description: Test supplied residuals, including round-trip residuals, against a declared tolerance and report a breach, without asserting that any chain is exactly reversible.
inputs: Declared tolerance value, unit and the party that set it
Supplied residual or round-trip deviation values
Chain reversibility characteristics such as iteration, grid interpolation and rounding
outputs: Tolerance breach verdict with observed maximum residual
Round-trip claim code with the reasons exactness is not claimed
preconditions: A tolerance is declared with a unit and an owner
Residuals were supplied; this function does not compute coordinates to obtain them
effects: Reports breach or conformance against the declared tolerance
Refuses to emit an exact round-trip claim for non-bijective, iterative or rounded chains

functions.name: Report chain outcome and consumer disclosures
functions.description: Compose the transformation report: one outcome status, the exception set, the accuracy and uncertainty summary, lineage pointers to the original geometry and CRS, and any lossy-export or round-trip qualification.
inputs: Verdicts from applicability, epoch, resource-pin, normalization and tolerance checks
Accuracy and uncertainty summary
Original geometry and CRS references
Export or serialization losses that were applied
outputs: Consumer disclosure set including the unknown-accuracy flag and lossy-export notes
preconditions: All contributing checks have produced a verdict or an explicit not-evaluated marker
effects: Emits a report with a single outcome status and an observation timestamp
Does not enforce acceptance, gate downstream use, or write an audit trail; those belong to the adopting Dimension

composition.purpose: Place this mixin inside the parent spatial-context model as its coordinate-expression specialization. The parent keeps place identity and spatial-context semantics; this model adds only geometry, referencing, operation lineage and coordinate quality. The parent boundary was not supplied as a relation rationale and remains under review.

composition.target: Host subject model requiring located geometry
composition.purpose: Attach geometry, CRS reference, coordinate epoch, operation lineage and quality statements to a host subject without asserting the host's identity, lifecycle, authority or permissions.

composition.target: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset (IOGP) and equivalent geodetic parameter registries
composition.purpose: Cite CRS, operation, method, parameter, extent and stated-accuracy definitions by code or URI, and record the dataset version pinned. The registry owns those definitions and their deprecation and supersession lifecycle; this model carries references and subject-specific pins only.

composition.target: ISO 19111 / OGC Abstract Specification Topic 2 referencing-by-coordinates conceptual schema
composition.purpose: Use the standard's vocabulary for coordinate operation, conversion, transformation, concatenated and point-motion operation, coordinate epoch, operation accuracy and domain of validity. Alignment only; conformance is not claimed without recorded evidence.

Carry an engine name and version as a reproduction pin, together with the binding needed to rebuild the declared chain. The engine owns execution, run-time candidate ranking, resource resolution and its own release lifecycle; none of that is modelled here.

composition.target: Geodetic grid and deformation-model distribution service
composition.purpose: Carry resource identity, version and content checksum, plus the availability state observed. Hosting, licensing, redistribution and retraction of resources remain with the distributor.
Bind accuracy and uncertainty values to a specific geometry and chain using external quality vocabulary. Measure definitions, evaluation procedures and conformance levels stay in the quality model.

composition.target: Encoding and interchange profiles for geospatial data
composition.purpose: Map inline data onto encoding rules for CRS reference, axis order, coordinate epoch, precision and antimeridian handling, and record which rule was applied as a treatment declaration. Encodings own their serialization constraints.

owner_package_requirements: Name an owner for the geometry and coordinate-reference mixin, and name the geodetic authority whose registry dataset version the Dimension pins as its default.
Declare the default transformation engine and its version, the default resource distribution source, and the policy for accepting or refusing ballpark and null operations.
Publish the Dimension's default coordinate tolerance, retained precision and required disclosure set, and the named purposes against which fitness is asserted.
Record jurisdictional and licensing constraints on grids, deformation models and methods that the Dimension may reference but may not redistribute.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use governed identifiers for everything defined elsewhere: registry codes or definition URIs of the form http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/{authority}/{version}/{code} for coordinate reference systems and operations, and distributor-issued names plus version labels for grid and deformation resources. Mint identifiers in the Dimension's own namespace only for records this model owns, namely chain declarations, derived-geometry lineage entries and transformation reports.
registry_links: Geodetic parameter registry supplying CRS, operation, method, parameter, extent and accuracy definitions, with the pinned dataset version recorded.
Definition-resolution service for coordinate reference system and operation URIs used in interchange.
Grid and deformation-model distribution catalogue supplying resource names, version labels and checksums.

canonicalization_rules: Order chain steps by ascending step index; the applied order, not the storage order, is canonical.
Normalize axis order and ordinate units to the endpoint CRS definitions before any comparison of two chains or two geometries.
Express coordinate epochs as decimal years with the convention stated; express record timestamps as RFC 3339 date-times normalized to UTC for comparison while retaining the recorded offset.
Express identifiers in their governed form (registry code or definition URI); compare coordinates only at the declared resolution, never at full stored precision.
patch_rules: A chain declaration is immutable once any outcome or derived geometry references it; corrections are issued as a new declaration with a supersession pointer to the old one.
Correcting an accuracy, uncertainty or outcome value requires a new observation timestamp and a recorded basis; overwriting in place is not permitted.
Adding a resource, engine or registry pin that was previously absent is a correction of the record, not of the result, and must not be presented as improving the result's accuracy.
Never re-derive a geometry silently to satisfy a patch; a new derivation produces a new derived geometry with its own lineage.
compatibility_rules: Adding optional accuracy, uncertainty, resource-pin or treatment fields is backward compatible.
Changing the default axis order, default retained precision, default tolerance or the aggregation rule for chain accuracy is a breaking change and requires a version increment and re-disclosure.
Removing or repurposing a resource pin, an operation version label or a lineage reference is breaking, because previously reproducible records stop being reproducible.
Widening an exception code's meaning is breaking; introducing a new, narrower exception code alongside the existing set is not.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the thing being identified: the geodetic registry's coordinate-operation, method or CRS code for definitions, and the distributor's resource name plus published version label for a grid, triangulated-network or deformation-model resource.
Governed global identifier or IRI where no master-system code exists, such as an OGC definition URI for a coordinate reference system or operation, used in its full resolvable form.

UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only for records this model itself owns, namely chain declarations, derived-geometry lineage entries and transformation reports, and never as a substitute for an available registry code or distributor identifier. A date, a coordinate epoch, a dataset year or a version date is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record every record-level time as an RFC 3339 date-time that includes seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Where they differ, record event time (when the geometry or position was valid in the world) separately from observation or ingestion time (when the chain was evaluated, the pins were taken and the outcome was recorded); a transformation report always carries an observation time. A coordinate epoch is a distinct decimal-year value that qualifies coordinates in a dynamic reference frame and is never stored as, compared with, or substituted for an RFC 3339 timestamp.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Grid, triangulated-network, deformation-model and registry-dataset artifacts are serial and are named {authority-or-distributor}:{resource-name}:{version-label}. A version label is never reused for changed content: any change of content checksum requires a new version label. Locally produced transformation reports are not serial and take a Dimension-assigned identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every reference to a serial resource must carry a content checksum with a named algorithm. A chain declaration whose resource checksum cannot be verified must be reported as unverified rather than treated as reproducible, and a checksum mismatch is a recorded exception, not a silent substitution. Integrity values are recorded and compared here; production, hosting and revocation of the resources themselves belong to the distributor.

policies: Never claim conformance to ISO 19111, an EPSG guidance note or any national geodetic standard without recorded evidence; record alignments and record conflicts explicitly.
Never present a ballpark, null or copy operation as accurate. An unquantified step forces an unknown-accuracy declaration for the whole chain, and that declaration must reach the consumer.
Always preserve the original geometry and its original coordinate reference system and epoch when a derived geometry is stored; a derived geometry never replaces its original.

Do not promise exact round trips. Chains involving grid interpolation, iterative methods, dimensionality changes or stored-precision rounding are not bijective, and any reversibility claim must be bounded by a declared tolerance.
Licensing and jurisdictional restrictions travel with a resource reference; reference restricted grids and methods, do not copy their content into this model.
State fitness only against a named purpose, and disclose the exception set, uncertainty and lossy-export notes with it.

read: Reading a chain declaration returns the declared pins as recorded; it never recomputes a result or re-resolves an operation against a newer registry version.
Resolve CRS and operation references against the registry dataset version pinned on the record, and report divergence if the current registry version differs.
Reading a derived geometry must also surface its original geometry reference, outcome status and unknown-accuracy flag.
create: Create a chain declaration only with resolvable source and target CRS references, an explicit step order with directions, and an explicit ballpark flag.
Create a derived-geometry lineage entry only with references to the original geometry, the original CRS and epoch, and the chain declaration used.
Create a transformation report only with a single outcome status and an observation timestamp; a report without a status is not a valid record.
update: Chain declarations are append-only once referenced; issue a superseding declaration rather than editing in place.
Accuracy, uncertainty and outcome values may be corrected only with a recorded basis, a new observation timestamp and retention of the superseded value.
Resource, engine and registry pins may be completed after the fact but must be marked as retrospectively added and must not change the recorded outcome.
delete: Deletion of this model's own records (chain declarations, derived-geometry lineage entries and transformation reports) is by tombstone: retain the identifier, source and target CRS references, resource and toolchain pins, outcome status and supersession pointer, and remove only payload detail.
Retain a lineage entry for at least as long as any derived geometry that cites it is retained; deleting lineage while keeping the derived geometry is prohibited because it destroys interpretability.
Never delete an original geometry, its CRS reference or its epoch in order to retain a derived geometry.

Erasure scheduling, legal hold, disposition execution and proof of destruction are owned by the adopting Dimension's retention policy and by the referenced records-retention model; this model declares the tombstone shape and the minimum retention dependency, and neither executes deletion nor holds the audit trail of it.

Referenced grid, deformation-model and registry definitions are never deleted by this model; withdrawal of a resource is recorded as an availability state on the pin, and disposition of the resource itself belongs to its distributor.

roles.name: Geodetic authority (external)
responsibilities: Define and version coordinate reference systems, operation methods, parameter values, extents and stated accuracies, and manage their deprecation and supersession.
Publish the dataset versions and guidance that adopting Dimensions pin against.

roles.name: Dimension geometry owner
responsibilities: Set the Dimension's default CRS, tolerance, retained precision, disclosure set and pinned registry dataset version.
Decide whether ballpark or fallback operations may be accepted, and for which named purposes.

roles.name: Transformation recorder
responsibilities: Record chain declarations with complete endpoint, epoch, method, parameter, direction and resource pins.
Record derived-geometry lineage entries that keep the original geometry and CRS recoverable.

roles.name: Quality reviewer
responsibilities: Review accuracy, uncertainty, precision and outcome declarations for internal consistency and for honesty about unknowns.
Reject records that assert exact round trips, hide a ballpark step or omit the unknown-accuracy flag.

roles.name: Consumer or integrator
responsibilities: Read the outcome status, exception set and disclosure notes before relying on a derived geometry.
Re-derive from the original rather than chaining further operations onto an already derived geometry when accuracy matters.

access.default_rule: Geometry, coordinate reference, operation lineage and quality records are readable by any role that may read the host subject. This mixin inherits the host's access decision and must never widen it; where the host restricts precise location, the restriction applies to every derived geometry, extent and bounding box produced from it.
exceptions: Precise coordinates for protected sites, protected species locations or identifiable persons may be generalized for a wider audience, but the generalization must be recorded as a derived geometry with its own lineage, treatment code and inflated uncertainty, never as a silent edit of the original.

Licensed grid, triangulated-network and deformation-model content may be referenced by identity, version and checksum but not redistributed; access to the resource itself is governed by its distributor's licence.
Resource pins and engine versions may be readable when the coordinates they qualify are not, so that reproducibility can be assessed without disclosing location.
A bounding box or extent derived from restricted geometry is itself restricted at the same level.
audit_requirements: Record which role created, superseded or tombstoned each chain declaration, lineage entry and transformation report, with the observation timestamp.
Record the registry dataset version, engine version and resource checksums in force at the time of recording, so a later dispute can be resolved against what was actually used.
Record retrospective completion of pins distinctly from original recording.
The audit trail itself is stored and evaluated by the adopting Dimension's audit facility; this model supplies the fields and does not own audit-trail semantics or retention.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL, Processes URL, Owner and the pinned registry dataset version.
Read the specification at the Specification URL to learn the bundle, layer and finding structure, the identity priority and the exclusive artifact rule.
Read the storage-type document and the interface document before reading or writing any record, since both are projections and neither defines semantics.
Read the processes document before creating, superseding or tombstoning a chain declaration, lineage entry or transformation report.
Resolve every coordinate reference system and operation reference against the pinned registry dataset version before interpreting any coordinate.

coverage.claim: This structure covers the coordinate-referencing, coordinate-operation, accuracy and outcome surface of WM-XCT-033 to the depth supported by the cited primary standards, registry publications and geodetic-agency material. Endpoint binding, epoch handling, operation classification, method and parameter pins, resource and toolchain pins, lineage preservation, stated accuracy, positional uncertainty, axis and unit normalization, dimensionality change, geometry-level treatment and explicit outcome declarations are each grounded in at least one primary source. Densification tolerance, polar and singularity handling, and the aggregation rule for chain-level accuracy are marked as gaps because no consulted primary source specifies them normatively. No claim of completeness is made for host-subject geometry semantics, raster or coverage regridding, or non-consulted national geodetic regimes.

checklist.notes: Endpoints, methods, operations and resources are identified by registry code, definition URI or distributor name plus version; Dimension-assigned identifiers are restricted to records this model owns, and dates and epochs are explicitly barred from acting as identifiers.

Chain declarations are append-only with supersession; registry deprecation and supersession state is cited, not owned. The lifecycle of CRS and operation definitions belongs to the geodetic registry and is recorded as a boundary.

Step-to-operation, chain-to-endpoint, derived-to-original and record-to-resource relationships are all modelled as references; the composition ledger separates aligned registries from referenced engines and distributors.
Coordinate epoch is modelled as a decimal-year qualifier of coordinates and kept strictly separate from RFC 3339 record timestamps, with event time distinguished from observation time.
Registry dataset version, engine version, resource version and checksum, and derivation timestamps are all pinned; lineage sufficiency is itself a validation question.

Roles separate the external geodetic authority, the Dimension geometry owner, the recorder, the reviewer and the consumer. Definition ownership, execution ownership and resource ownership are all placed outside this model.
Applicability, epoch, pin integrity, normalization and tolerance checks are functions that validate and report; the outcome finding fixes a single status and a named exception taxonomy.
The mixin inherits and never widens the host's access decision; generalization of protected locations must become a recorded derived geometry, and derived extents inherit restriction.

Tombstone shape, minimum retention dependency between lineage and derived geometry, and the prohibition on deleting an original are stated here; scheduling, legal hold and disposition execution are explicitly assigned to the adopting Dimension's retention policy.

CRS by reference, definition URIs, storage CRS, axis-order authority, epoch carriage and encoding-driven antimeridian and precision rules are grounded in three independent encoding and API standards, with their conflicts recorded rather than harmonized away.
Registry-stated operation accuracy, per-point local error estimates from grid-based transformations, and the mandatory unknown state for ballpark or unquantified steps are all modelled and separated.
Method, parameter, direction, resource checksum, engine and registry pins together with original preservation give an explicit reproducibility verdict rather than an implicit assumption.

Antimeridian splitting and coordinate precision have a primary basis in RFC 7946, but densification tolerance and polar or singularity handling rest on practice; no consulted primary source specifies them normatively, so the finding is marked as a gap rather than presented as canonical.

No consulted source defines how to combine per-step stated accuracies into one chain figure. The model requires the rule and its conservatism assumption to be declared locally and labelled a local computation, not an authority statement.

Deliberately excluded. Functions calculate, validate or report only; execution, resource acquisition, gating of downstream use and audit-trail construction belong to referenced engines, distributors and the adopting Dimension.

known_omissions: No primary source was found that normatively specifies a densification tolerance rule or polar and projection-singularity handling; both are recorded as declarations with an explicit gap marker.

ISO 19157-1 data-quality text was not retrievable at an openly accessible URL, so positional-quality vocabulary is aligned indirectly through the referencing standard's operation-accuracy concept and through agency uncertainty material rather than cited directly.

The EPSG guidance notes 7-1, 7-2, 7-5 and 7-6 were not machine-extractable at fetch time; only the authoritative guidance-note index with titles, versions and dates is cited, so formula-level and null-transformation detail is acknowledged rather than quoted.
Vertical datums, geoid models and the conversion between ellipsoidal and orthometric heights are treated only as a dimensionality and height-type boundary, not as a modelled subject.
Raster and coverage regridding, resampling kernels and pixel-centre conventions are out of scope; only vector geometry is addressed.
Uncertainty correlation between neighbouring vertices of one geometry is not modelled; only per-coordinate or per-operation values are carried.
The parent model WM-XCT-010 boundary is asserted from registry metadata alone, since no relation rationale was supplied.
conflicts: A fixed-CRS encoding requires longitude-latitude order and a single reference system, while CRS definitions carry their own axis order and any CRS may be referenced by URI in other profiles. A record can be valid under one and contradict the other, so the axis-order authority must be recorded explicitly.

The concept of a ballpark transformation is an engine-level classification with no matching formal class in the referencing standard; the registry expresses comparable cases as null or copy transformations. This model treats it as a declared status rather than a standard class.

One encoding recommends splitting geometries that cross the antimeridian, while other encodings and engines permit spanning geometries and use an inverted bounding box. No single normative rule applies across encodings, so treatment is recorded per record.

A registry states one scalar accuracy per operation, whereas grid-based national transformations supply per-point local error estimates. Combining the two into a single figure is not standardized and is flagged as a local computation.

Carrying a coordinate epoch for a dynamic storage CRS is a recommendation in one API standard but is structurally required by another encoding when a dynamic CRS is referenced; requirement strength differs and the model takes the stricter reading.
regional_assumptions: The geodetic-agency evidence used here is United States specific, covering a national spatial reference system, its grid-based horizontal and vertical transformations and its plate-fixed frame family. Other jurisdictions maintain their own frames, grids, tools and accuracy conventions, and none of the region-scoped statements generalize.

Grid and deformation-model resources carry different licences by jurisdiction; availability from a public distribution network does not imply a right to use, and a Dimension must record its own licensing position.
Decimal-year epoch conventions, and the treatment of leap seconds when converting between a timestamp and an epoch, differ between agencies and are not harmonized here.
Transformations are region-scoped: a national transformation set spans a fixed set of regions and is undefined outside them, so area-of-use testing is mandatory rather than advisory.
adversarial_checks: Checked every bundle, layer, finding and function against the composition ledger: none owns CRS or operation definitions, none owns registry deprecation or supersession, none executes a transformation, acquires or licenses a resource, enforces acceptance, or constructs an audit trail. Where such a concept appeared, it was moved to out_of_scope, a boundary note or a REFERENCE link.

Stress-tested the round-trip temptation: grid interpolation, iterative methods, dimensionality reduction and stored-precision rounding each break bijectivity, so the model forbids an exact reversibility claim and permits only a tolerance-bounded one with the reasons stated.

Searched for a counterexample to the assumption that accuracy is always available: ballpark, null and copy operations have unknown accuracy by construction, so the unknown-accuracy flag is mandatory rather than optional and must propagate to the chain.

Verified that a coordinate epoch is never used as an identifier, never used as a record timestamp, and never conflated with event or ingestion time, since a decimal year and an RFC 3339 instant are different value kinds with different authorities.

Rejected an attractive but unsupported structure: a local mirror of registry operation definitions and their accuracy statements. It would fork registry-owned content, so those findings are reference-only with an explicit dataset version pin instead.

Tested the mixin boundary against widening: checked that no access, retention or lifecycle statement here can grant more visibility or longer life to a derived geometry than the host subject allows, and that derived extents and bounding boxes inherit the host's restriction.

Checked that a chain that succeeds numerically but leaves the declared area of use, loses a height ordinate on export, or depends on a missing grid still produces a qualified rather than a clean outcome status.
